question: The chronological progression found within global fossil records suggests that life forms over time have generally become more simple in structure and less diverse.

[EVOLUTIONARY EVIDENCE ANALYSIS] A student analyzes the anatomical wing of a bat and the flipper of a whale. 1) Identify the structural classification of these limbs and explain what they reveal about evolutionary history. 2) State two specific reasons why the fossil record alone cannot provide a perfectly continuous line of evidence for this relationship.
rubric: To score full points, the structural analysis must state: 1) These are homologous structures (specifically pentadactyl limbs). Even though they serve different functions (flying vs. swimming), their underlying anatomical similarities reveal that bats and whales descended from a shared common ancestor. 2) The fossil record has limitations due to missing links because: first, many ancient organisms were soft-bodied, decomposed, or were eaten before they could be fossilized; second, many fossils are buried in completely inaccessible areas or suffer physical damage over time, reducing the probability of discovery.
